fitSummary.verdict: 2× front_load_washer instances + one minimal integration domain represent 19/21 W1 procedures without distortion. Two procedures require platform-overlay handling (MEMS) or additional W1 compartment-attribution evidence — not integration-domain expansion. No verified behavior requires a third functional subsystem or a FlexWash-shaped ontology blob.
fitSummary.verifiedW1Coverage: 19/21 procedures fit without distortion under tested model
fitSummary.integrationDomainAbsorptionRisk: low — candidate did not grow to absorb ordinary wash functions

minimalityResult.summary: All three discovery responsibilities are evidenced, but cross_compartment_coordination may reduce to a dependency on inter_instance_communication health plus instance metadata — not a separate orchestration surface at freeze time. System supervision (SF) fits integration domain better than FL_LOWER.control_board alone, but shares diagnostic entry with primary supervisory PCB — one integration domain still sufficient.

inter_instance_control_communication.reason: AC7 cannot fit FL_LOWER or FL_UPPER alone without distortion

system_supervision.reason: SF is appliance-level System Error — not compartment-local; mapping to single control_board loses system scope

cross_compartment_coordination.reason: Independent compartment operation proven; simultaneous active wash not proven; AC7 upper-enable dependency may be modeled as integration comm failure inhibiting FL_UPPER without separate orchestration node

minimalityResult.reducibleTo: inter_instance_communication + system_supervision + instance_scoped_enable_inhibit (facet of integration domain, not second canonical node)

freezeReadiness.rationale: W1 fit partially passes with no unexplained integration-level behavior, but single-witness discipline prohibits freeze. MEMS platform gap and compartment-attribution gaps on 1 procedure are W1 evidence gaps, not architecture rejection.
